Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

missSBM (development version)

Changes in the estimation

  • block-node and block-dyad sampling: the SBM part is now fitted on the observed dyads, with the sampling term in the update of the blocks, as was already the case for node and dyad. Under these designs the sampling only depends on the blocks, so that the missing dyads are ignorable given the blocks: they are now integrated out exactly, instead of being approximated by a variational distribution independent of the blocks, q(Z) q(Y_miss). This is a tighter lower bound of the same likelihood, not a new criterion. It also removes a feedback loop: the imputations of the missing dyads, computed from the blocks, entered the update of the blocks, and the dyads between two unobserved nodes, never observed, fed back on themselves (the connectivity of a block of unobserved nodes could drift to 0, and classes collapsed when exploring larger numbers of blocks, e.g., the 196 blogs of frenchblog2007 up to 18 blocks). The results of these two designs change. In simulations (n = 200, Q = 3), the mean ARI goes from 0.65 to 0.94 for block-node (42% of observed nodes) and from 0.32 to 0.88 for block-dyad (30% of observed dyads).
  • The ICL is now built on the observed data, for all the designs: the observed dyads and the sampling matrix, the missing dyads being integrated out. It is -2 times the variational lower bound maximized by the algorithm, evaluated at the MAP memberships (each node in its most probable block, as the classification likelihood of Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert), plus the penalty; the same for the ICL of the fitted SBM alone (fittedSBM$ICL). For the designs whose sampling only depends on the blocks (dyad, node, covar-*, block-node, block-dyad), and for double-standard, the missing dyads are integrated out exactly. For degree, the bound includes the expected log-likelihood and the entropy of the imputations. (During the development of this version, the ICL was the bound minus the entropy of the soft memberships: under degree, whose imputations, computed from the memberships, make them near-hard, this rewarded degree, chosen in 20% to 75% of the cases under node and block-node sampling; at the MAP memberships, the designs are on an equal footing, #55.) The ICL of the previous versions added the expected log-likelihood of the imputed dyads, without their entropy, as if the missing dyads were classified: as the imputations are computed by the model, this rewards purer blocks with no data behind them, and favors more blocks, the more so as more dyads are missing. In simulations (inst/simus/PR48-block-designs/), the true number of blocks is selected in 95% to 100% of the cases in 11 settings out of 12 (it was 0% to 100%), and the ICL now picks the design that generated the data among node / block-node and dyad / block-dyad (it preferred block-node and double-standard in most cases). The selected models of all the designs can change.
  • The penalty of the ICL built on the observed data counts the observed dyads for the connectivity of the SBM (and the effects of the covariates), estimated on them, instead of all the possible dyads (#51), as sbm does for a network with missing values. The sampling parameters still count all the dyads (or all the nodes): the sampling matrix is fully observed. The penalty of each connectivity parameter decreases by -log(rate of observed dyads), e.g. 1.9 at 15% of observed dyads. In simulations (inst/simus/PR51-penalty/, 800 networks near the detectability threshold, Erdos-Renyi included), the selected number of blocks changes for 13 networks, all toward the true one, and no structure is found in Erdos-Renyi networks with either penalty; the campaign of #48 is unchanged. New field nbObservedDyads of the fitted SBM.
  • The ICL of the previous versions, built on the network completed by the imputations, is no longer available (it was kept as missSBM_param(ICL = "completed") during the development of this version, and is removed in #51): it has no justification, and it would not reproduce former results anyway, as the estimation of all the MNAR designs has changed. To reproduce former results, install missSBM 1.1.0 (e.g., remotes::install_version("missSBM", "1.1.0")). With a single block, block-node and node, or block-dyad and dyad, still give the same ICL.
  • The VEM monitors (and stops on) the bound it maximizes, loglik, for all the designs. For dyad, node and covar-*, it monitored the expected log-likelihood of the network completed by the imputations of the SBM plus their entropy, which is not the bound: the fits of these designs can stop at a different iteration (in simulations, same selected number of blocks, ICL differences without direction).
  • degree sampling (#55): the VEM maximizes the bound of the model again (factorized q(Z) q(Y_miss), bound of Jaakkola and Jordan), as in Tabouy, Barbillon & Chiquet (2020). Since missSBM 1.0.0, its SBM part was fitted on the observed dyads, ignoring the sampling (the clustering was that of node sampling), and its sampling part given the SBM part: no single objective was maximized. It is now fitted in three stages, each stopping on the objective it increases: the SBM part on the observed dyads, the sampling part given the SBM part, then the coordinate ascent of the bound in all the variables, the blocks and the connectivity being updated on the network completed by the imputations (new internal class SimpleSBM_fit_degree). The sampling part, which only involves the missing dyads, is iterated to convergence given the SBM part (in stage 2 and at each M-step of stage 3), as the EM of double-standard: with the default threshold, one step per iteration stopped it early. Started from the usual initialization, this coordinate ascent reaches worse local optima; from the first two stages, it increases the bound in every simulated network and keeps the partition. In simulations (inst/simus/issue55-degree/, n = 200), the ICL chooses degree when it generated the data in 100% of the cases for a medium or strong effect of the degree (0% to 20% before), 20% for a weak one, and in 5% of the cases without effect of the degree; in the campaign of #48, degree is chosen in 90% of the cases under degree sampling (0% before), the true design in 95% under node and 60% under block-node (the two designs are close for an assortative network). The monitoring of a degree fit has a column stage.
  • double-standard sampling (#52): the missing dyads are also integrated out given the blocks, instead of being approximated by imputations independent of the blocks. A dyad between blocks q and l is missing with probability m_ql = pi_ql (1 - p1) + (1 - pi_ql) (1 - p0): this term enters the update of the blocks, and the connectivity and (p0, p1) are estimated jointly, by an EM on the missing dyads iterated to convergence at each M-step, in Q x Q. The previous version made one step of this EM per iteration of the VEM, which stopped long before convergence (after 2 iterations with the default threshold): p1 was underestimated (0.53 for 0.8, n = 200, Q = 3). In simulations (n = 200, Q = 3, 6 replicates per setting), the ARI goes from 0.73 to 0.92, from 0.85 to 0.98 and from 0.96 to 0.99 for (p0, p1) = (0.6, 0.3), (0.5, 0.5), (0.2, 0.8), (p0, p1) are estimated without bias, and the true number of blocks is always selected. Among dyad, block-dyad and double-standard, the ICL now picks double-standard in 100% of the cases when it generated the data (60% before, see inst/simus/PR48-block-designs/). No imputation of each missing dyad is stored any more: imputedNetwork averages the posterior given the blocks over the memberships.
  • double-standard with a single block: (p0, p1) are only identified through the differences of connectivity between the blocks. With a single block, the observed data only inform pi p1 and (1 - pi) p0: the model is fitted with p0 = p1, i.e. as dyad sampling (same ICL), with one sampling parameter in the penalty, and estimateMissSBM() warns when vBlocks contains 1.

Memory and speed (#49)

  • No n x n matrix is formed any more for the designs without covariates: the imputations are not computed along the VEM of the designs that integrate the missing dyads out (they are computed on demand by imputedNetwork, at the final parameters), and at the missing dyads only, in C++; the network object is built by reading the dense input in C++, without masks; the initial clustering uses no matrix of distances. At n = 4000 (inst/simus/issue49-memory/), building the network object takes +95 Mb instead of 5 times the input (+574 to 715 Mb), the initial clustering +91 to 128 Mb instead of +526 to 672 Mb, and the fit of node, block-dyad and double-standard +4 to 110 Mb instead of +301 to 637 Mb; the whole estimation is about twice as fast. Same results (up to rounding for the imputations).

Bug fixes

  • degree sampling: the imputations of the missing dyads were not probabilities (the logistic function had been dropped from their update in 2018, so that they were the linear predictor truncated to [eps, 1 - eps]), and the sampling parameters were estimated on wrong degrees (the observed edges were left out of the imputed network since 1.0.0, and only one triangle of an undirected network was read). The estimates of the sampling parameters and the imputations of this design are now correct; the SBM part is still fitted on the observed dyads, which is more robust than plugging the imputations of the dyads between unobserved nodes, as these are never observed.
  • imputedNetwork no longer doubles the imputations with the degree sampling.
  • degree sampling, bound of Jaakkola and Jordan: the variational parameter zeta_i, at its optimum sqrt(E[(a + b D_i)^2]), often above 1, was truncated to [eps, 1 - eps] like a probability (since 2018). The estimates of (a, b) and the imputations were biased, the more so as the effect of the degree is strong (b underestimated by 15% for a strong effect, n = 200; now 0.6%; inst/simus/issue55-degree/). Also, the expected log-likelihood of the sampling, used in the ICL, plugged the expected degrees into log logistic(a + b D_i), which is above its expectation (Jensen), instead of the bound of Jaakkola and Jordan that the updates maximize: the ICL of degree now uses this bound.
  • block-dyad sampling: the expectation of the log-likelihood of the sampling was computed as the log of the expected sampling probabilities, log(Z psi Z’), instead of the expectation of the log (since 2018). The updates of the parameters were right, but the objective monitored by the VEM and the ICL were overestimated (by 5 to 20 on the ICL of networks with 200 nodes). The estimates are unchanged in our simulations, but the selected number of blocks can change.
  • block-node and block-dyad sampling: the sampling parameters, indexed by the blocks, were not permuted with the blocks of the SBM when these are reordered at the end of the VEM, so that fittedSampling$parameters (and coef()) did not match the blocks of fittedSBM, and polish() added a permuted sampling term to its gains. The ICL was not affected. A side effect: this permuted term acted as a random perturbation that could get polish() out of a local optimum, so that a fit at a fixed number of blocks without exploration can now end elsewhere.

Minor changes

  • degree sampling: the sampling part is computed on the sparse pattern of the missing dyads, in O(n + number of missing dyads) memory instead of several dense n x n matrices. Same results up to rounding errors (checked against the dense formulas in the tests).
  • The observed nodes of an undirected network are found without building R | t(R), a nearly full sparse matrix when most dyads are observed. This was done for every fit with a node-centered sampling, including each candidate of the exploration: about 18% faster overall on a network with 2000 nodes, same results.

missSBM 1.1.1

Bug fixes

  • Force sequential execution (nbCores = 1) in the blockmodels-based reference tests, avoiding a segfault caused by blockmodels’s internal parallel::mclapply use, which is unsafe when combined with macOS’s Accelerate/vecLib BLAS-LAPACK framework (observed on CRAN’s r-oldrel-macos-arm64 check machine).

missSBM 1.1.0 (2026-07-21)

CRAN release: 2026-07-21

Major changes

  • Breaking: estimateMissSBM()’s control must now be built with the new missSBM_param() (one named, defaulted argument per option) instead of a raw list(...), which now errors with a message pointing at the replacement.
  • missSBM_fit now exposes split(), merge(), candidates_split() and candidates_merge() as instance methods, previously inlined in missSBM_collection’s exploration logic; same search algorithm, now independently testable.
  • new polish(control) (missSBM_fit and missSBM_collection): node-swap refinement after VEM convergence, fixing individually misclassified nodes that split()/merge() cannot reach.
  • requesting more blocks than a network actually supports can make VEM collapse one or more classes; this used to be silent, and split/merge exploration’s own repair of it could silently corrupt vBlocks’s bookkeeping (duplicated/missing entries, non-smooth ICL/ELBO in plot()). Now fixed and made visible: missSBM_fit$repair(control) recovers a collapsed fit ; new occupiedBlocks/ degenerate fields expose any remaining collapse; bestModel skips degenerate models when possible and plot() marks them with a distinct point shape; estimateMissSBM()’s new stopOnDegenerate/maxConsecutiveDegenerate controls (default TRUE/2) stop forward exploration from growing further into a persistently unsupported range.
  • new estimate_chain() (missSBM_collection) / warmChain control (default FALSE, opt-in): initializes each model by splitting the already-converged, smaller neighbor instead of an independent cold clustering, substantially reducing collapse in practice, at the cost of fitting vBlocks sequentially rather than in parallel.
  • replace the NLopt/CCSAQ optimizer for the covariate connectivity parameters with a builtin Newton-Raphson solver (the M-step objective is concave, so it converges reliably in a handful of iterations); nloptr is no longer a dependency
  • fix partlyObservedNetwork$imputation(): the fill value for missing dyads was biased low by including not-yet-imputed entries in its own computation. Known side effect: doubleStandardSampling_fit’s initial psi bootstrap can degenerate when the fill value exactly matches the empirical observed edge rate (refined away by the VEM loop that follows)

Minor changes

  • profiled estimateMissSBM() and fixed several hot-path inefficiencies: avoidable dense * sparse promotion overhead, a redundant recomputation of the dense imputed-network matrix, and an ifelse() evaluating both of its branches unconditionally. Roughly 3x faster on our benchmark, bit-identical results
  • estimateMissSBM() now sorts/de-duplicates vBlocks if needed (with a warning), since exploration and chaining both assume it is strictly increasing.
  • estimateMissSBM()’s control drops the exploration field: nobody used "forward"/ "backward" alone at that level, only "both"/"none", so iterates now doubles as the on/off switch (0 disables exploration entirely). missSBM_collection$explore() no longer reads a stored exploration control field either; its direction argument (default "both") is now a plain per-call parameter, still available for advanced/internal use.
  • cap the number of merge candidates tried during backward exploration (control$maxMergeCandidates, default 30) instead of always trying every pair
  • fix a crash and a closed-form algebra bug in the “degree” sampling design; parameter recovery for this design can still be biased under heavy missingness (known limitation)
  • fix a consistency bug in missSBM_fit$doVEM()’s step-back: only the SBM was restored, not the sampling model or the current imputation
  • speed up getCovarArray() and kmeans_missSBM()’s seeding
  • remove unused src/utils.h
  • missSBM_fit’s polish(), repair(), candidates_split() and candidates_merge() gain the same default control as doVEM(), so they can be called standalone without building a full control list first; missSBM_collection’s calls (which always pass an explicit control list) are unaffected ; missSBM_collection’s estimate()/polish()/explore() now share a control list stored at construction, no longer requiring control on every call.
  • Factored missSBM_collection’s explore_forward()/explore_backward() into a shared private explore_direction(), and missSBM_fit’s candidates_split()/candidates_merge()’s trial-fit loop into a shared private trial_fit_candidates(); verified bit-identical output on the same fixed-seed scenario used throughout this changelog to diagnose VEM collapse

missSBM 1.0.0 [2021-05-25]

CRAN release: 2021-05-25

  • now rely on future_lapply for parallel computing (plan to be set by the user)
  • faster model exploration (used to be called ‘smoothing’), now integrated by default in estimateMissSBM
  • Use sparse Matrices to encode 0 and NAs
  • complete rewriting of optimization routines (E and M steps) with C++ armadillo routines
  • Better initialization and embedded C++ kmeans implementation
  • important bug fix in MAR case
  • bug fix in inference on covariates
  • bug fixed in blockDyad-sampling
  • missSBM::SimpleSBM_fit_missSBM now inherits from from sbm::SimpleSBM rather than sbm::SimpleSBM_fit
  • change field ‘netMatrix′to′netMatrix' to 'networkData’ to comply with new interface in sbm
  • defunct functions estimate, sample and simulate are no longer supported
